source_excerpt: RUDRAPRAYAG: Uttarakhand CM Pushkar Singh Dhami on Monday criticised Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge over his remarks about Prime Minister Narendra Modiâs father and accused Samajwadi Party chief Akhilesh Yadav of using the term âinfiltratorsâ to describe the people of Uttarakhand. Responding to the remark, Kharge said, âModi ka baap bhi jayega.âDhami also criticised Akhilesh Yadav over his alleged use of the term âinfiltratorsâ in reference to the people of Uttarakhand, pointing to his association with the Congress leadership.âMeanwhile, Akhilesh Yadav, who is in an alliance with the Congress and is a close friend of Rahul Gandhi, has used the term infiltrators in reference to the people of Uttarakhand,â Dhami said.The chief minister also referred to incidents of police firing during the Uttarakhand statehood movement. He alleged that Akhilesh Yadavâs father had ordered firing on statehood protesters while serving as Uttar Pradesh chief minister. Referring to incidents in Khatima, Mussoorie, Shriyantra Tapu and Rampur Tiraha, Dhami said, âWhat else could we expect from him?âPointing out that Akhilesh Yadavâs wife is from Uttarakhand, Dhami said the Samajwadi Party chief should exercise restraint while speaking about the stateâs people.âHis own wife hails from Uttarakhand. He should, at the very least, refrain from using such language,â Dhami said.He also questioned the Congressâs continued alliance with the Samajwadi Party and called on its leadership to clarify its position.âFurthermore, the Congress party is in an alliance with him; they must decide what they value more, this alliance or the self-respect of Uttarakhand,â he said.Rudraprayag bridge-tunnel project to be inaugurated soonDuring his visit to Rudraprayag on Monday, Dhami inspected a newly constructed bridge-and-tunnel project developed under the Char Dham road initiative. After reviewing the work, he said the infrastructure would be formally inaugurated soon.Built at an estimated cost of Rs 156 crore, the project includes a 200-metre bridge over the Alaknanda River and a 900.30-metre tunnel. Including the approach roads, the route extends for around 1.18 km and connects the Kedarnath National Highway (NH-107) with the Badrinath National Highway (NH-07).Vehicles began using the route on a trial basis on Monday. Once regular traffic starts after the formal inauguration, pilgrims travelling to Kedarnath and Badrinath will be able to bypass the congested main market in Rudraprayag.The bypass is expected to ease traffic congestion in the town during the Char Dham Yatra, providing relief to residents and pilgrims. Dhami said improving road connectivity and developing modern infrastructure were key priorities for the state government, as better transport links could also support local businesses, tourism and employment.He also reviewed slope stabilisation and protection work along landslide-prone stretches of the Rudraprayag-Gaurikund National Highway. The measures are intended to reduce landslide risks and improve the safety and resilience of the pilgrimage route.Dhami donates 150 books to Sangam LibraryThe chief minister also visited the Sangam Library, where he praised the district administrationâs âDonate a Book, Plant a Tree of Knowledgeâ campaign, led by District Magistrate Vishal Mishra.The initiative aims to encourage reading among students, make study material available to candidates preparing for competitive examinations and strengthen local libraries. The campaign has collected more than 2,500 books covering competitive examinations, general knowledge, literature and other subjects.Dhami contributed 150 books to the collection. Addressing the gathering, he said books played an important role in acquiring knowledge and developing personality. He added that community-led book donation initiatives could help students who lacked access to study material and encourage a stronger reading culture among young people.Mishra said the collected books were being made available to students and other readers, particularly those preparing for competitive examinations. He added that efforts were under way, with public participation, to develop local libraries into centres for learning and study.Dhami announces plan to raise sanitation workersâ honorariumEarlier in the day, Dhami attended a Shobha Yatra organised by the Dehradun Municipal Corporation to mark Maharishi Valmiki Prakatotsav. During the event, he announced that the honorarium paid to sanitation workers employed across various state departments would be increased soon. He said a meeting would be held shortly to finalise the decision.Paying tribute to Maharishi Valmiki on his birth anniversary, Dhami said the sage had introduced the world to the life and ideals of Lord Shri Ram through the Ramayana. He said Valmikiâs life demonstrated how noble thoughts and righteous actions could inspire others.Dhami added that a personâs identity was shaped by knowledge, conduct and contribution to society, and said Maharishi Valmiki had inspired the vision of an egalitarian society free from discrimination.Highlighting the teachings of the Ramayana, the chief minister said the epic conveyed enduring values such as truth, righteousness, sacrifice and duty. He said its message encouraged people to uphold love, equality, fraternity and human dignity.He also said that a person should be judged by character and actions rather than caste or social status, adding that Sanatan culture emphasised mutual respect, harmony and social cohesion.Dhami said India was pursuing development while preserving its cultural heritage under Prime Minister Narendra Modiâs leadership. He cited the construction of the Ram Temple in Ayodhya and the recognition of figures such as Maharishi Valmiki, Nishadraj and Mata Shabari within the temple complex as examples of efforts to promote social harmony and inclusive cultural traditions.He also noted that Ayodhyaâs international airport had been named after Maharishi Valmiki. The chief minister said the central government was working to bring poor and marginalised communities, including Scheduled Castes, Scheduled Tribes and other backward classes, into the mainstream.Citing schemes such as the PM Awas Yojana, Ujjwala Yojana, Ayushman Bharat, Jal Jeevan Mission and free ration distribution, Dhami said these initiatives had helped crores of families improve their living conditions. He also highlighted legal measures aimed at safeguarding the rights of SC and ST communities and preventing atrocities against them.Reiterating the importance of equal opportunities and dignity for all, Dhami said the Uttarakhand government was committed to improving the lives of disadvantaged sections of society.He described Uttarakhand as Devbhoomi, a land shaped by the spiritual traditions of sages, faith in sacred shrines and ancient cultural practices. He said the state government aimed to protect this heritage while pursuing modern development, passing traditional values on to younger generations and ensuring equal opportunities for all.
